evidence: Cic. Brut. 293: quam sī testimōnium dīcerēmus
Ter. Ph. 293: neque testimōnī dictiō est
terms.comment: To give evidence: testimōnium dīcere (Cic.); against someone, testimōnium dīcere in aliquem (Traupman 195, 311). A witness is testis; to bear witness, testificārī, frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Sall. Jug. 35.6: indicium profitētur (M-O s.v. turn state’s evidence)
terms.comment: Indicium profitērī, to turn informer (Traupman 195; M-O).

phrases.latin: vidē nē religiō nōbīs tam adhibenda sit quam sī testimōnium dīcerēmus
phrases.english: take care: we may need to be as scrupulous as if we were giving evidence

phrases.latin: tum quī testimōnium dīceret ut arbitrārī sē dīceret etiam quod ipse vīdisset
phrases.english: and that a witness should say “I think” even of what he had seen himself
